title: Part I Protheoria: Two classes of controversy — Melanchthonian AC vs Bergen Formula party
pass_a_gloss: Controversiarum Classes duae with Augustana Confession Theologians. Class 1: with genuine Luther disciples professing AC even as Melanchthon recognized it after Wittenberg Concord, often explained esp. Art. x. Nearly only contested head left: Lord's Supper — Melanchthon in later Confess. (Variata by Philip's private authority): Body & Blood truly exhibited with bread & wine to those eating. Prior 1530 edition: Body & Blood truly present & distributed, plus disapproval of otherwise-thinkers — that one apple of discord (μῆλον ἔριδος) while Luther lived, first with Carlstadt, then Helvetians Zwingli/Oecolampadius and those who joined Reformers. Class 2: with disciples of Brenz, Andreae, Flacius Illyricus, Hunnius, etc., and all who subscribed Torgau Articles first written 1576 — chief architect Jakob Andreae of Tübingen — soon (few changes) referred into Book of Concord / Bergen Formula 1577, published 1580 after subscriptions arose. In this Ubiquity / Majesty of Christ's Human Nature already set in the citadel; only prior AC 1530 admitted, which they call Invariata! Also definitive sentences on controversies then among Lutherans (Flaccians, Wittenbergers, Osiandrists) and with so-called Calvinists — including Predestination, yet explained so that the sole cause of salvation and thus of election is placed in God, not in us.
pass_b_english: Of the Controversies with the Theologians of the Augsburg Confession, two various Classes are to be set up. For some are with the genuine Disciples of Luther, and with those who profess the Augsburg Confession even as Melanchthon recognized it after the Wittenberg Concord, and as it was often explained, especially as to Article X. And now almost the only contested head remaining is the Lord's Supper — Melanchthon expressing the presence of Christ's Body in these words in the later Confession, which others call the Variata by Philip's private authority: That with the bread and wine the Body and Blood of Christ are truly exhibited to those who eat in the Lord's Supper. The prior edition, of the year 1530, had: That the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present, and are distributed to those who eat in the Lord's Supper, with the disapproval of those who think otherwise added. That one thing was, while Luther lived, an apple of discord (μῆλον ἔριδος) — first with Carolostadius, from what was said before, and then also with the Swiss, Zwingli, Oecolampadius, and those who joined them in the order of the Reformers.

Others intervene with the disciples of Johann Brenz, Jakob Andreae, Matthias Flacius Illyricus, Aegidius Hunnius, and others, and as many as subscribed the Torgau Articles, first written in the year 1576 — Jakob Andreae, the Tübingen Theologian, being their chief architect — soon to be referred (with few changes) into the Book of Concord, or Bergen Formula, of 1577, published in 1580 after the subscriptions had arisen. And in this the dogma of Ubiquity, or the Majesty of Christ's Human Nature, is already set in the citadel; and only the prior Augsburg Confession of the year 1530 is admitted, which they call the Unaltered! But other definitive sentences also are expressed in that Book concerning Controversies then agitated among the Lutherans themselves — for example Flaccians, Wittenbergers, Osiandrists, and so on — and likewise with those they call Calvinists. Among which is that concerning Predestination, yet explained there so that the sole cause of salvation, and therefore also of election, is placed in God, not in us.
source_text: Controversiarum cum Augustanae Confessionis Theologis variae constituendae Classes duae. Quaedam enim sunt cum genuinis Lutheri Discipulis, ac professis Augustanam Confessionem, etiam ut a Melanchthone recognita fuit, post Concordiam Wittenbergensem, ac saepius explicata, in specie quoad Artic. x. Ac jam solum fere caput controversum remanet de Cena Domini; praesentiam Corporis Christi efferente his verbis Melanchthone, in posteriori Confessione, quam alii Variatam dicunt privata auctoritate Philippi: Quod cum pane & vino vere exhibeantur Corpus & Sanguis Christi vescentibus in Cena Domini. Habuerat editio prior, Anni 1530. Quod Corpus & Sanguis Christi vere adsint, & distribuantur vescentibus in Cena Domini, addita improbatione secus sentientium. Quod unum vivo Luthero fuit μῆλον ἔριδος, primo cum Carolostadio, ex ante dictis, deinde & cum Helvetiis, Zwinglio, Oecolampadio, ac qui his accesserunt in Reformatorum ordine. Aliae intercedunt cum discipulis J. Brentii, Jac. Andreae, M. Flaccii Illyrici, Aegid. Hunnii, &c. & quotquot subscripsere Torgensibus Articulis, scriptis primo A. 1576. Praecipuo horum architecto Jacobo Andreae Tubingensi Theologo, mox (paucis mutatis) referendorum in Librum Concordiae, seu Formulam Bergensem, A. 1577. vulgatam A. 1580. post exortas subscriptiones. Et in hac jam dogma de Ubiquitate, seu Majestate Naturae Hum. Christi in arce collocatum; admissaque etiam sola Confessio Augustana prior, Anni 1530. quam invariatam vocant! Sed & aliae sententiae definitivae in eo Libro expressae, de Controversiis, ut inter ipsos Lutheranos tum agitatis, puta Flaccianos, Wittenbergenses, Osiandristas, &c. sic & cum Calvinianis quos vocant. Quas inter illa de Praedestinatione, sed sic ibi explicata, ut sola salutis causa adeoque & electionis ponatur in Deo, non in nobis.
